name: REPAIR (RNA Editing for Programmable A-to-I Replacement)
therapeuticGoalDescription: Correct pathogenic RNA mutations by programmable adenosine-to-inosine (A→I) editing using a catalytically inactive Cas13b fused to ADAR2.
molecularDefect: Pathogenic adenosine-containing variants correctable through A→I editing at the RNA level.
diseaseMechanism: A guide RNA directs catalytically inactive Cas13b (dCas13b) fused to the ADAR2 deaminase domain to a target RNA, enabling site-specific A→I editing without altering genomic DNA.
suitableVariantTypes: Missense variants; nonsense variants; splice-site variants; pathogenic G→A mutations amenable to A→I correction.
typicalDiseases: Proof-of-concept studies in monogenic disorders; proposed for neurological, retinal, and metabolic diseases. No approved therapeutic applications.
rnaTargetRegion: Exonic or splice-site regions complementary to the guide RNA.
transcriptRequirement: Presence of an editable adenosine within a guide-accessible RNA region.
typicalLength: Guide RNA typically ~30–80 nt; Cas13b–ADAR2 delivered separately.
designRules: Design guide RNA to position the target adenosine within the editing window; optimize guide length and mismatch placement; validate editing by RNA sequencing.
secondaryStructureRequirement: Accessible RNA target region to permit guide RNA binding and Cas13 recruitment.
offTargetConsiderations: Bystander A→I editing; guide RNA-dependent off-target binding; Cas13-associated specificity considerations.
advantages: Programmable editing; reversible; no genomic DNA modification; adaptable to multiple RNA targets.
limitations: Requires delivery of a large fusion protein; currently preclinical; potential off-target editing; no approved therapies.

references.paper: REPAIR: Programmable A-to-I RNA Editing with CRISPR-Cas13 by Cox et al., Nature (2017)

references.usedFor: Comparative review of programmable RNA editors.
